newsitem.title: CANADA: Snowstorm seen for Red River Valley April 19 - EC.
newsitem.headline: Snowstorm seen for Red River Valley April 19 - EC.

text.p: A snowstorm was forecast for Manitoba's Red River Valley on April 19, a meteorologist said.

"Our U.S. weather model has another storm moving through South Dakota to Lake Superior and it may affect the head waters of the Red River on the weekend of April 19th," Environment Canada meteorologist Henry Schmidt told Reuters.
EC's European weather model, however, forecast a snow storm for Nebraska on the weekend of April 5 but none in Manitoba for the weekend of April 19, Schmidt added.
The April 19 storm forecast could be off by 100 miles and a day, he cautioned.
Winnipeg saw a record-breaking blizzard over the weekend that dumped 57.4 cms (23 inches) of snow on the Red River Valley, raising the risk of record spring flooding, officials said.
Manitoba's Red River Valley produces wheat, barley, canola, corn and flax.
It represents about two percent of Prairie acreage but 3.5 percent of production due to good yields, the Canadian Wheat Board has said.
